Both should remain visible so that a later method does not convert missing
information into an assumed favorable value.

For this study, @tbl-represented-problem provides the minimum useful
problem description. It contains enough identity and context to reconstruct
the comparison, expose
legal changes, and recognize when the representation is no longer useful. A
longer-lived or more consequential use needs more retained history and source
identity. The rules for claims that leave the project belong to the later
discussion of decision responsibility.

The chapter's distinctions now come together in one problem description.

| **Part of the Problem** | **Representation for the Lighthouse Cache Study** |
| --- | --- |
| Architecture question and permitted change | For comparison `XR-L2-CAP-A` at design revision `XR-COMPUTE-A`, determine which, if either, of the 3\ MiB and 4\ MiB settings should advance against a rerun 2\ MiB baseline. Only `l2.capacity` may change. Its legal values `2MiB`, `3MiB`, and `4MiB` map to `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, and `L2-4M-A`; the first is the rerun baseline. |
| Fixed hardware, software, and workload state | Cache policy `CACHE-POLICY-A`, associativity, NoC `NOC-A`, memory system `MEMSYS-A`, the 2\ GHz microarchitecture, compiler `COMPILER-A`, runtime `RUNTIME-A`, and RISC-V software image `SW-BASE-A` remain fixed. Workload `XR-TRACE-A` must resolve to a retained snapshot with stable frame identifiers and boundaries, its collection policy, coverage, and owner. The configuration, generator revision, generated cache instance, and linked implementation collateral must also remain aligned. |
| Exact source and version identities | The comparison definition, design revision, candidate configurations, fixed hardware and software, workload snapshot, cycle-level simulator `SIM-A`, cache model `CACHE-A`, power model `PM-A`, SRAM model `SRAM-A`, and PVT assumptions `PVT-A` each require an exact source, version or hash, and owner. Timestamps, regeneration, or consistency checks establish freshness where needed. These remain specification identities because this prospective example retains no source package or execution artifacts. |
| Constraints and checks | Each candidate must identify versioned reference behavior, testbench or properties, coverage intent, interface and reset assumptions, and required checks. Modeled subsystem dynamic plus leakage power must not exceed 3\ W, cache macro area 1.5\ mm^2^, or modeled access time 2.5\ ns. Thermal and IR-drop reviews remain independent later checks. |
| Observations, history, and acquisition cost | The execution history is initially empty. The budget permits four cycle-level executions including infrastructure reruns and one SRAM evaluation per capacity. Each attempt retains status, cost, raw returns, and derived fields. A prior result becomes a comparable sample only when its design, candidate, hardware, software, workload, tool-model, and PVT identities match; other results remain advisory context. |
| Cross-layer relationships | Capacity can change miss behavior and the frame-time distribution. It also changes macro organization and may affect power, area, access time, and physical integration. Candidate results must remain linked to the workload, software, cache policy, memory system, generated artifact, constraints, and checks that give those effects meaning. |
| Blind spots and known unknowns | The representation contains no retained floorplan, congestion result, workload snapshot, completed thermal or IR-drop review, or evidence that `XR-TRACE-A` covers every deployed condition. It may miss effects outside the named tools. Open questions include whether either larger cache improves 99th-percentile frame time enough to advance and whether later physical review exposes an omitted effect. |
| Useful scope and handoff | The representation supports this cache-capacity comparison and selection of at most one candidate for later RTL evaluation. It excludes changes to cache policy, prefetching, coherence, NoC, compiler, software scheduling, floorplanning, thermal or IR-drop signoff, security, reliability, and product cost. It passes @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization an inspectable problem, not a complete model of the XR subsystem or a selected method. |

: **The represented problem makes the cache comparison inspectable.** It
connects exact design and workload identities, legal changes, checks, history,
freshness, and limits without selecting a method or claiming a result.
{#tbl-represented-problem tbl-colwidths="[24,66]"}

The first four groups define the comparison and its checks. The next two retain
what was observed and connect each observation to the architecture relationships
that produced it. The final two expose unsupported inferences and bound the
handoff. The decisive link maps `l2.capacity` to one realizable cache
configuration while the workload, software, cache policy, memory system, and
constraints remain tied to every comparison.

In a future execution, the fields may live in several project systems. What
matters is that every retained artifact refers to the same study, design
version, workload version, and candidate. A directory full of individually
valid files is not a represented problem if no one can tell which files
describe the same comparison.

### Inputs to Method Choice

@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization needs an inspectable problem,
not a prescribed technique. The Lighthouse problem description therefore
passes forward the source-linked state developed throughout the chapter.
@tbl-represented-problem summarizes the worked Lighthouse problem, while the
earlier sections supply its sample conditions and acquisition cost, checked
data and failures, connected native and learned representations, and the blind
spots and freshness limits that bound their use.

It intentionally contains no proposed next candidate, predicted consequence,
surrogate, optimizer, acceptance threshold for a model, or execution result.
Those additions would answer questions this chapter has not yet asked.
@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization can now decide whether the
work should proceed directly to tools or add a method. If an added method is
justified, the study first names the engineering job, then chooses a method
family (generation, prediction, or optimization) or a justified combination,
together with a conventional, learned, or hybrid implementation.
@sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces can decide how the chosen work
is connected to tools. @sec-feedback-verification-trust can decide what
feedback means. The order protects the study from being reshaped around the
first available method.

The handoff is inadequate if it cannot reproduce or identify the current
design, if it hides a controlling hardware-software or physical relationship,
if its legal actions bundle undeclared changes, if its sources disagree without
a resolution, or if no one can state where the representation is useful.

## Open Research Questions

The central open problems concern acquiring costly and incomplete architecture
data, preserving design relationships across representations, and keeping
project knowledge current.

**Building architecture datasets.** Architecture data comes from sources with
different costs, coverage, failure modes, and authority.

- **How can synthetic and low-fidelity data expand coverage without hiding
  unsupported regions?** Progress can be measured by held-out error,
  calibration, and missed legality or feasibility boundaries against stronger
  observations, reported separately by design and workload region.

- **How should an architecture team retain and use failed and censored runs
  without treating local failure as a universal boundary?** Failed tools,
  infeasible candidates, limit violations, and unknown outcomes carry different
  information. Their meaning remains conditional on the design, workload, tool
  path, and constraints that produced them. Censoring-aware regression and
  failure-aware acquisition can be judged by feasibility-boundary error,
  calibration, candidate-selection quality, and tool calls saved against
  deletion and naive-label baselines.

**Preserving relationships and testability.** Representations and study
releases expose some architecture relationships while hiding or distorting
others.

- **How can learned representations capture useful similarity without hiding
exact architecture constraints?** Identity, hierarchy, topology, order, units,
legality, uncertainty, and check results may not survive in one learned
vector. The representation must support generalization while still permitting
exact constraints to reject an invalid candidate. Evaluation should jointly
measure held-out transfer and illegal-candidate rejection against flat or
unconstrained representations.

- **How can architecture claims derived from private data remain independently
  testable?** Progress would let an outside group reproduce declared aggregate
  statistics, rerun a public subset through the released harness, and recover
  the stated claim limits without access to restricted artifacts.

**Keeping project knowledge current.** Broad prior knowledge is useful only
when current design state can correct it.

- **How can an automated method detect that represented project state no longer
describes the artifact it names?** Regeneration can catch drift when one source
owns the build, but hand edits, generated collateral, external tools, and
delayed results create additional divergence paths. The remaining challenge is
detecting meaningful staleness without capturing and rechecking the entire
project continuously. Injected project changes make the tradeoff measurable
through stale-state detection recall, false alarms, invalid tool runs prevented,
and checking cost.

## Conclusion

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Preserve exact facts before learning from them"}
Architecture data remains useful only when its source, design and workload
identity, units, conditions, cost, and limits survive dataset construction and
representation. A learned representation may add capability, but it does not
replace the native artifact or current project state that later checks must
inspect.
:::

Architecture data is not a collection of interchangeable labeled examples.
Specifications, code, RTL, traces, formal results, tool reports, rejected work,
and reviews carry different information. Workloads determine which behavior is
exercised, and every stored result remains tied to the design, software, tool,
conditions, and acquisition cost that produced it. Coverage matters more than
row count.

A usable dataset makes those dependencies inspectable. It aligns source
identities and units, checks versions and lineage, preserves failures and
censored results, separates tool problems from measured design violations, and
documents held-out designs, access limits, omissions, and leakage risks. This
work turns heterogeneous sources into data that a later method can use without
making unsupported comparisons look clean.

Data does not replace project knowledge or live state. A foundation model can
supply broad prior knowledge, and retrieval can bring source-linked material
into the current task. The checked-in design, software image, workload,
constraints, unresolved issues, and accepted results still come from current
project sources. A state that cannot identify or reproduce the artifact it
names is not current.

Native artifacts, typed structures, graphs, sequences, spatial forms, retrieved
text, and learned representations each expose different properties. Embeddings
can support useful similarity and adaptation, but identity, hierarchy,
topology, order, legality, units, exact constraints, uncertainty, and returned
check results remain linked outside them. The architect chooses connected
representations that preserve the relationships controlling the current
question and expose what remains missing.

The chapter's output is the represented problem in
@tbl-represented-problem. It contains source identity, workload, sample
conditions and cost, checked data, current state, legal changes, dependencies,
history, linked representations, freshness, blind spots, and known unknowns for
the Lighthouse cache study. It does not determine how to explore that problem.
That source-linked description gives method choice a firm starting point.
@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization can decide whether to proceed
directly to tools or add prediction, generation, optimization, or a
conventional or hybrid combination without inventing missing state.
